title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Price increase (4.5%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in two recent weeks (96 and 104 units) vs baseline 96.5; no uplift observed. Noise-adjusted effect of price hikes is near zero.

drivers.name: Supply delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note only. No past data on supply risk affecting demand. Low confidence. Adds downside uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.5. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 4.5% above regular, which historically correlates with lower demand. The 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 weeks had the same price (10.32) and sold 96 and 104 units—very close to baseline (96.5), suggesting no lift. The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is not significant. Supplier delivery warning introduces supply risk, which may reduce demand if stockouts occur. This is a single, vague signal. No past data shows demand drop from supply issues. The classical model suggests no effect, which aligns with recent price behavior. Thus, the median stays at 1.0, but downside risk is added.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.5 | 5%-95%: 62.7 - 233.7 | 10%-90%: 67.2 - 191.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
